stem: A uniform rod of length 2a is placed horizontally on the edge of a table. Initially the centre of mass of the rod is at a distance a/3 from the edge. The rod is released from rest. If the rod slips after it has turned through an angle θ, find the coefficient of friction between the rod and the table. —

The uniform slender rod AC has a mass m and is pinned at B, with AB = L/3 and BC = 2L/3. If it is released from rest when θ = 0° (rod horizontal), determine the magnitude of the reactive force exerted on it by pin B when θ = 90°. —

Steel tape is being wound onto a spool which rotates with a constant angular velocity ω 0 . Denoting by r the radius of the spool and tape at any given time and by b the thickness of the tape, derive an expression for the acceleration of the tape as it approaches the spool. —

A circular hole of radius r/2 is cut from a circular disc of radius r. The disc lies in the xy-plane and the hole is cut so that its rim passes through the centre of the disc. Determine the moment of inertia of the remaining body about an axis passing through the centre of the original disc and perpendicular to the plane of the disc, in terms of the mass m of the remaining body. —

A uniform solid spherical ball of mass M and radius R is projected along a rough horizontal surface (coefficient of kinetic friction μk) so that initially (t = 0) it slides with a linear speed v₀ but does not rotate. As it slides, it begins to spin and eventually rolls without slipping. How long does it take to begin rolling without slipping?

A square frame is made of four uniform rods, the mass of each rod being m and its length l. Match the axis of rotation in Column-I with the moment of inertia about it in Column-II. Column-I: (A) axis in the plane of the frame through one corner, parallel to a diagonal (frame held as a diamond, horizontal axis through the top vertex); (B) axis along one side of the frame; (C) axis along a diagonal; (D) axis perpendicular to the plane of the frame through the mid-point of one side. Column-II: (P) (2/3)ml² (Q) (5/3)ml² (R) (7/3)ml² (S) (8/3)ml². (a) (A)-(S), (B)-(Q), (C)-(P), (D)-(R) (b) (A)-(P), (B)-(Q), (C)-(R), (D)-(S) (c) (A)-(S), (B)-(P), (C)-(Q), (D)-(R) (d) (A)-(R), (B)-(S), (C)-(P), (D)-(Q)

Multiple Correct Answer Question. Two uniform equal ladders AB and AC, each of weight W, lean against each other and a string is tied between E and F. They stand on a smooth horizontal surface. Then: (a) the force exerted by one rod on the other at A is equal in magnitude to the tension T in the string (b) tension T = (W/2)cotθ (c) the normal reactions at B and C are equal (d) the normal reaction at B or C is greater than W —
book_key: a, c force at A = T; N B = N C = W

stem: A uniform solid cylinder of mass m and radius R, spinning with angular velocity ω₀ in the sense shown (its lowest point moving down the slope), is lowered onto a rough inclined plane of angle 30° with the horizontal, μ = 1/√3. The cylinder is released (from rest, translationally) at a height of 3R above the horizontal. Find the total time taken by the cylinder to reach the bottom of the incline.

The solid ball of radius r and mass m rolls without slipping down the 60° trough shown (the two faces of the trough meet at 60°, and the trough itself is inclined at 45° to the horizontal). Determine its angular acceleration. —

A hinged construction consists of three rhombuses (with corresponding sides parallel, so all three have the same angles) whose sides are in the ratio 5 : 3 : 2, the left vertex A₀ being hinged to a fixed wall. Vertex A₃ moves in the horizontal direction at a velocity v. Velocity of A₂ is : (a) 2.5 v (b) 1.5 v (c) (2/3)v (d) 0.8 v

In Column-I certain situations are depicted. In all cases there is a uniform solid cylinder on a rough plank, the plank resting on a smooth floor. Assume friction is sufficient for pure rolling. The mass of the cylinder is equal to that of the plank. Match with appropriate descriptions in Column-II. Column-I: (A) horizontal force F (to the right) applied at the top of the cylinder; (B) a clockwise couple applied on the cylinder; (C) horizontal force F (to the right) applied at the centre of the cylinder; (D) horizontal force F (to the right) applied on the plank. Column-II: (P) Plank accelerates to the left (Q) Friction on cylinder is towards right (R) Friction on cylinder is in direction opposite to its acceleration (S) The acceleration of cylinder is greater in magnitude than that of the plank (T) Acceleration of cylinder is towards right. (a) (A)-PQST, (B)-PQT, (C)-RST, (D)-QT (b) (A)-PQT, (B)-PQRT, (C)-RST, (D)-QT (c) (A)-PQST, (B)-PQT, (C)-QT, (D)-RST (d) (A)-PQRST, (B)-PRS, (C)-RST, (D)-QT

Inside a uniformly accelerating thin-walled spherical shell of radius R, which is rolling on a horizontal surface, there is a small body slipping around (it stays on the rear side, as shown). Angle of friction between body and inner surface of sphere is 23°. Which of the following can be the acceleration 'a' of the centre of sphere to ensure that the small body stays at R/2 distance from the surface? (a) g/√3 (b) 3g/4 (c) g tan23° (d) g√3/2

A solid cylinder is placed in "ends on" position on an inclined plane. It is found that at an angle θ the cylinder starts to slide. When the cylinder is turned on its side and allowed to roll, it is found that the steepest angle at which the cylinder performs pure rolling is φ. The ratio tanφ/tanθ is: (a) 1/3 (b) 1 (c) 3 (d) 1/2 —

A solid sphere is given an angular velocity ω and kept (with no linear velocity) on a rough fixed inclined plane; as shown in the figure the spin is clockwise, the incline rising to the right, so the contact point slides DOWN the incline. Choose the correct statement(s). (a) If μ = tanθ then sphere will be in linear equilibrium for some time and after that pure rolling down the plane will start. (b) If μ = tanθ then sphere will move up the plane and frictional force acting all the time will be 2mg sinθ (c) If μ = tanθ/2 there will never be pure rolling (consider inclined plane to be long enough) (d) If incline plane is not fixed and it is on smooth horizontal surface then linear momentum of the system (wedge and sphere) can be conserved in horizontal direction.
book_key: d horizontal momentum of wedge + sphere is conserved

stem: The spool shown in figure is placed on a rough horizontal surface and has inner radius r and outer radius R. The angle θ between the applied force F (applied tangentially to the inner drum) and the horizontal can be varied. The critical angle (θ) for which the spool does not roll and remains stationary is given by: (a) θ = cos −1 (r/R) (b) θ = cos −1 (2r/R) (c) θ = cos −1 √(r/R) (d) θ = sin −1 (r/R) —

A billiard ball (uniform solid sphere of mass M, radius R) initially at rest is given a sharp blow by a cue stick. The force is horizontal (along +x) and is applied at a distance 2R/3 below the centreline, as shown in figure. The initial speed of the ball is v₀ and the coefficient of kinetic friction is μk. Choose the correct statement(s). (a) Initially kinetic friction acts in −î direction (b) Initially kinetic friction acts in î direction. (c) Ball instantaneously starts pure rolling. (d) Initial angular velocity of ball is 5v₀/(3R)
book_key: c Ball instantaneously starts pure rolling ⚠

stem: A uniform rod AB of weight W is movable in a vertical plane about a smooth hinge at A, and is sustained in equilibrium by a force P acting along a string BCP passing over a smooth peg C as shown, AC being vertical. If AC is equal to AB, and θ is the base angle of the isosceles triangle ABC, then the force P is: (a) W/cosθ (b) W cosθ (c) W/sinθ (d) W sinθ —

In the arrangement shown, a spool of mass m and moment of inertia I (inner radius R, outer radius 2R) rests with its outer rim on a plank of mass M lying on an incline of angle θ. A rope wound on the inner drum leaves it on the side facing the plank and is tied, parallel to the incline, to a fixed wall at the top. Friction between the spool and the plank is sufficient to prevent sliding; there is no slipping of the rope. The system starts from rest. Column-I: (A) When m > M and there is no friction between the plank and the inclined surface. (B) When M > m and there is no friction between the plank and the inclined surface. (C) When m = M and there is no friction between the plank and the inclined surface. (D) When m = M and the friction coefficient between the plank and the inclined surface is tanθ. Column-II: (P) Plank will ascend (Q) Plank will descend (R) Plank will remain stationary (S) Spool may rotate clockwise (T) Spool may rotate anticlockwise. (a) (A)-PS, (B)-QT, (C)-R, (D)-R (b) (A)-QT, (B)-PS, (C)-R, (D)-R (c) (A)-ST, (B)-RQ, (C)-R, (D)-R (d) (A)-PQ, (B)-ST, (C)-R, (D)-R

Two small balls A and B, each of mass m, are joined rigidly to the ends of a light rigid rod of length l. The system lies on a smooth horizontal table. A particle of the same mass moving with speed u perpendicularly to the rod strikes ball B. Consider the four situations and find the angular velocity ω of the rod after collision. Column-I: (A) rod lies freely, collision elastic; (B) rod hinged at its middle, collision elastic; (C) rod lies freely, colliding particle sticks; (D) rod hinged at its middle, colliding particle sticks. Column-II: (P) ω = u/l, (Q) ω = u/2l, (R) ω = 4u/3l, (S) ω = 2u/3l. Options: (a) A-P, B-R, C-Q, D-S (b) A-P, B-Q, C-R, D-S (c) A-R, B-P, C-Q, D-S (d) A-Q, B-S, C-P, D-R —

A uniform thin flat isolated disc is floating in space (initially at rest). It has radius R and mass m. A force F is applied to it in the y-direction at a distance d = R/2 from the centre (to the right of the centre, as shown). Treat this problem as two-dimensional. At the instant shown the: (a) acceleration of the center of the disc is F/m. (b) angular acceleration of the disk is F/mR. (c) acceleration of leftmost point on the disc is zero. (d) point which is instantaneously unaccelerated is the rightmost point.
book_key: a, b, c a cm = F/m, α = F/mR, leftmost point unaccelerated

stem: Multiple Correct Answer Question. A horizontal rod of mass 'M' and length L is tied to two vertical strings symmetrically as shown in the figure. One of the strings at end Q is cut at t = 0 and the rod starts rotating about the other end P. Then: (a) at t = 0, angular acceleration of the rod about P is 3g/2L (b) at t = 0, angular acceleration of the rod about the C.M. of the rod is 3g/2L (c) at t = 0, acceleration of the C.M. of the rod is 3g/4 in the downward direction (d) at t = 0, tension in the string at P is Mg/4. —
book_key: a, b, c, d all four statements are correct

stem: Multiple Correct Answer Question. A uniform bar of length 6a and mass 8m lies on a smooth horizontal table. Two point masses m and 2m moving in the same horizontal plane with speeds 2v and v, respectively, strike the bar (2m strikes downward at a point a to the left of the centre C, and m strikes upward at a point 2a to the right of C) and stick to the bar after collision. Denoting angular velocity, total energy and velocity of centre of mass by ω, E and V c respectively, we have after collision: (a) V c = 0 (b) ω = 3v/5a (c) ω = v/5a (d) E = 3mv²/5 —
book_key: a, c, d V c = 0, ω = v/5a, E = 3mv²/5

stem: A spool (consider it as a double uniform disc system of total mass M and radius R, joined by a short tube of radius r at their centre) is placed on a horizontal surface as shown in figure. A light string wound several times over the short connecting tube leaves it tangentially from the lower side of the tube, runs horizontally and passes over a light pulley; a weight of mass m is attached to the end of the string. Find the acceleration of the falling mass m. Neglect the mass of the connecting tube and slipping of the spool (it rolls without slipping).

A uniform solid cylinder of radius R rolls over a horizontal plane passing into an inclined plane forming an angle α with the horizontal, as shown in figure. Find the maximum value of the velocity v 0 which still permits the cylinder to roll onto the inclined plane section without a jump. The sliding is assumed to be absent. —

Two masses M and m (M > m) are connected by a light string going over a pulley of radius r. The pulley is free to rotate about its axis which is kept horizontal. The moment of inertia of the pulley about the axis is I. The system is released from rest. Find the angular momentum of the system when the mass M has descended through a height h. The string does not slip over the pulley.

A small sphere of radius R is held against the inner surface of a larger sphere of radius 6R as shown in figure (the small sphere's centre level with the large sphere's centre). The masses of large and small spheres are 4M and M, respectively. This arrangement is placed on a horizontal table, the origin (0, 0) being the point where the large sphere initially touches the table. There is no friction between any surfaces of contact. The small sphere is now released. Find the coordinates of the centre of the larger sphere when the small sphere reaches the other extreme position.
book_key: (L + 2R, 0) — the large sphere's centre shifts 2R horizontally, its height unchanged

stem: A block of mass m 1 = 2 kg slides along a frictionless table with a speed of 10 m/s. Directly in front of it, and moving in the same direction, is a block of mass m 2 = 5 kg moving at 3 m/s. A massless spring with a spring constant 11.2 N/cm is attached to m 2 as shown in figure. When the blocks collide, what is the maximum compression of the spring? Assume that the spring does not bend. —

A uniform rod AB of mass 2 kg and length l = 100 cm is placed on a sharp support O such that AO = a = 40 cm and OB = b = 60 cm. A spring of force constant k = 600 N/m is attached to end B and to the floor below, as shown in figure. To keep the rod horizontal, its end A is tied with a thread (to the floor) such that the spring is elongated by y = 1 cm. Calculate the reaction of the support on the rod just after the thread is burnt. (g = 10 m/s²)

A ball of mass m moving with velocity v 0 experiences a head-on elastic collision with one of the spheres of a stationary rigid dumbbell as shown in figure. The mass of each sphere equals m/2, and the distance between them is l. Disregarding the size of the spheres, find the angular momentum of the dumbbell in the reference frame moving translationally and fixed to the centre of mass of the dumbbell. —

answer: F ≈ 1.13 × 10³ N (printed key 1100 N = same to 2 s.f.)
stem: The mechanism shown in figure is used to raise a wooden box of mass 50 kg. A string is wrapped around a cylinder that turns on an axle. The cylinder has radius 0.25 m and moment of inertia 0.92 kg m² about the axle. The force F is applied tangentially to the rotating crank handle, at a distance 0.12 m from the axle. What magnitude of the force F is required to raise the box with an acceleration of 0.80 m/s²? Neglect the moment of inertia of the axle and the crank. (g = 9.8 m/s²)

The center of a disk of radius r and mass m is attached to a spring of spring constant k, inside a ring of radius R > r as shown in the figure. The other end of the spring is attached on the periphery of the ring. Both the ring and the disk are in the same vertical plane. The disk can only roll along the inside periphery of the ring, without slipping. The spring can only be stretched or compressed along the periphery of the ring, following the Hooke's law. In equilibrium, the disk is at the bottom of the ring. Assuming small displacement of the disc, the time period of oscillation of center of mass of the disk is written as T = 2π/ω. The correct expression for ω is (g is the acceleration due to gravity): (a) √[(2/3)(g/(R−r) + k/m)] (b) √[2g/(3(R−r)) + k/m] (c) √[(1/6)(g/(R−r) + k/m)] (d) √[(1/4)(g/(R−r) + k/m)] (JEE Advanced 2025) —

A disc of mass M and radius R is free to rotate about its vertical axis as shown in the figure. A battery operated motor of negligible mass is fixed to this disc at a point on its circumference. Another disc of the same mass M and radius R/2 is fixed to the motor's thin shaft. Initially, both the discs are at rest. The motor is switched on so that the smaller disc rotates at a uniform angular speed ω. If the angular speed at which the large disc rotates is ω/n, then the value of n is _____ (JEE Advanced 2024) —

answer: a ω = 6.98 rad s⁻¹ and v = 4.30 m s⁻¹
stem: A bar of mass M = 1.00 kg and length L = 0.20 m is lying on a horizontal frictionless surface. One end of the bar is pivoted at a point about which it is free to rotate. A small mass m = 0.10 kg is moving on the same horizontal surface with 5.00 m s −1 speed on a path perpendicular to the bar. It hits the bar at a distance L/2 from the pivoted end and returns back on the same path with speed v. After this elastic collision, the bar rotates with an angular velocity ω. Which of the following statement is correct? (a) ω = 6.98 rad s −1 and v = 4.30 m s −1 (b) ω = 3.75 rad s −1 and v = 4.30 m s −1 (c) ω = 3.75 rad s −1 and v = 10.0 m s −1 (d) ω = 6.80 rad s −1 and v = 4.10 m s −1 (JEE Advanced 2023) —

Suppose there is a uniform circular disc of mass M kg and radius r m shown in figure. The shaded regions are cut out from the disc. The moment of inertia of the remainder about the axis A of the disc is given by (x/256)Mr². The value of x is _____. (Two circular holes of radius r/4 are cut out, their centres at a distance 3r/4 from the centre of the disc, the two radii to the holes making 135° with each other; A is the axis through the centre, perpendicular to the disc.) (JEE Main 2026 Shift 2) —

A uniform bar of length 12 cm and mass 20m lies on a smooth horizontal table. Two point masses m and 2m are moving in opposite directions with same speed of v and in the same plane as the bar, as shown in figure. These masses strike the bar simultaneously and get stuck to it. After collision the entire system is rotating with angular frequency ω. The ratio of v and ω is: (the 2m mass strikes 2 cm to the left of the bar's centre and the m mass 4 cm to the right of it) (a) 66 (b) 33 (c) 32 (d) 2√88 (JEE Main 2026 Shift 2) —

The pulley shown in figure is made using a thin rim and two rods of length equal to diameter of the rim. The rim and each rod have a mass of M. Two blocks of mass M and m are attached to two ends of a light string passing over the pulley, which is hinged to rotated freely in vertical plane about its center. The magnitudes of the acceleration experienced by the blocks is _____ (assume no slipping of string on pulley). (a) (M−m)g ÷ [(13/6)M + m] (b) (M−m)g ÷ [(8/3)M + m] (c) (M−m)g/(2M+m) (d) (M−m)g/(M+m) (JEE Main 2026 Shift 2) —

A uniform rod of mass m and length l suspended by means of two identical inextensible light strings as shown in figure. Tension in one string immediately after the other string is cut, is _______. (g acceleration due to gravity) (a) mg/4 (b) mg/2 (c) mg/3 (d) mg (JEE Main 2026 Shift 1) —

Two circular discs of radius each 10 cm are joined at their centres by a rod of length 30 cm and mass 600 gm as shown in figure. If the mass of each disc is 600 gm and applied torque between two discs is 43 × 10 5 dyne·cm, the angular acceleration of the discs about the given axis AB is _____ rad/s². (AB is perpendicular to the rod, 10 cm from one disc's centre and 20 cm from the other's) (a) 11 (b) 22 (c) 100 (d) 27 (JEE Main 2026 Shift 1) —

A thin uniform rod (X) of mass M and length L is pivoted at a height (L/3) as shown in the figure. The rod is allowed to fall from a vertical position and lie horizontally on the table. The angular velocity of this rod when it hits the table top, is ______ (g = gravitational acceleration) (a) (3/√2)√(g/L) (b) (1/√2)√(g/L) (c) √((3/2)(g/L)) (d) √(3g/L) (JEE Main 2026 Shift 2) —

Two masses 400 g and 350 g are suspended from the ends of a light string passing over a heavy pulley of radius 2 cm. When released from rest the heavier mass is observed to fall 81 cm in 9 s. The rotational inertia of the pulley is ____ kg·m². (g = 9.8 m/s²) (a) 4.75 × 10 −3 (b) 9.5 × 10 −3 (c) 1.86 × 10 −2 (d) 8.3 × 10 −3 (JEE Main 2026 Shift 1) —

The moment of inertia of a square loop made of four uniform solid cylinders, each having radius R and length L (R < L) about an axis passing through the mid points of opposite sides, is (Take the mass of the entire loop as M). (a) (3/4)MR² + (7/12)ML² (b) (3/8)MR² + (1/6)ML² (c) (3/4)MR² + (1/6)ML² (d) (3/8)MR² + (7/12)ML² (JEE Main 2026 Shift 1) —

Two masses m and 2 m are connected by a light string going over a pulley (disc) of mass 30 m with radius r = 0.1 m. The pulley is mounted in a vertical plane and it is free to rotate about its axis. The 2 m mass is released from rest and its speed when it has descended through a height of 3.6 m is _____ m/s. (Assume string does not slip and g = 10 m/s²) (JEE Main 2026 Shift 2) —

Two identical thin rods of mass M kg and length L m are connected as shown in figure (a T-shape: one rod hangs vertically from the point P at its top end, and the second rod is attached horizontally at the lower end of the first, at the horizontal rod's mid point). Moment of inertia of the combined rod system about an axis passing through point P and perpendicular to the plane of the rods is (x/12)ML² kg·m². The value of x is ______. (JEE Main 2026 Shift 1) —

A fly wheel (uniform disc) having mass 3 kg and radius 5 m is free to rotate about a horizontal axis. A string having negligible mass is wound around the wheel and the loose end of the string is connected to a 3 kg mass. The mass is kept at rest initially and released. Kinetic energy of the wheel when the mass descends by 3 m is ____ J. (g = 10 m/s²)

A uniform solid cylinder of length L and radius R has moment of inertia about its axis equal to I 1 . A small co-centric cylinder of length L/2 and radius R/3 carved from this cylinder has moment of inertia about its axis equals to I 2 . The ratio I 1 /I 2 is ______. (JEE Main 2026 Shift 2) —

A solid sphere of mass 5 kg and radius 10 cm is kept in contact with another solid sphere of mass 10 kg and radius 20 cm. The moment of inertia of this pair of spheres about the tangent passing through the point of contact is ______ kg·m². (a) 0.72 (b) 0.36 (c) 0.18 (d) 0.63 (JEE Main 2026 Shift 1) —

A solid sphere of radius 10 cm is rotating about an axis which is at a distance 15 cm from its centre. The radius of gyration about this axis is √n cm. The value of n is ______. (JEE Main 2026 Shift 1) —

A circular disc has radius R 1 and thickness T 1 . Another circular disc made of the same material has R 2 and thickness T 2 . If the moment of inertia of both discs are same and R 1 /R 2 = 2 then T 1 /T 2 = 1/α. The value of α is ______. (JEE Main 2026, 22 January Shift 1) —

Two cars A and B each of mass 10³ kg are moving on parallel tracks separated by a distance of 10 m, in same direction with speeds 75 km/h and 36 km/h. The magnitude of angular momentum of car A with respect to B is ______ J·s. (a) 2 × 10⁵ (b) 10⁵ (c) 3.6 × 10⁵ (d) 3 × 10⁵ (JEE Main 2026, 21 January Shift 2) —

When the position vector r̄ = xî + yĵ + zkˆ changes sign as −r̄, which one of the following vector will not flip under sign change? (a) Angular momentum (b) Velocity (c) Acceleration (d) Linear momentum (JEE Main 2026, 28 January Shift 2) —

answer: c Opposite to the direction of r̄
stem: If L̄ and P̄ represent the angular momentum and linear momentum respectively of a particle of mass m having position vector as r̄ = a(î cosωt + ĵ sinωt). The direction of force is (a) Opposite to the direction of L̄ (b) Opposite to the direction of L̄ × P̄ (c) Opposite to the direction of r̄ (d) Opposite to the direction of P̄ (JEE Main 2025 Online, 4th April Morning Shift) —

A force of 49 N acts tangentially at the highest point of a sphere (solid) of mass 20 kg, kept on a rough horizontal plane. If the sphere rolls without slipping, then the acceleration of the center of the sphere is (a) 2.5 m/s² (b) 3.5 m/s² (c) 0.25 m/s² (d) 0.35 m/s² (JEE Main 2025 Online, 3rd April Morning Shift) —

A uniform circular disc of radius R and mass M is rotating about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through its centre. A small circular part of radius R/2 is removed from the original disc as shown in the figure (the small disc touches the rim internally, its centre at R/2 from the centre O). Find the moment of inertia of the remaining part of the original disc about the axis as given above. (a) (17/32)MR² (b) (13/32)MR² (c) (9/32)MR² (d) (7/32)MR² (JEE Main 2025 Online, 22nd January Morning Shift) —

Moment of inertia of a rod of mass M and length L about an axis passing through its center and normal to its length is α. Now the rod is cut into two equal parts and these parts are joined symmetrically to form a cross shape. Moment of inertia of cross about an axis passing through its center and normal to plane containing cross is : (a) α/4 (b) α/8 (c) α (d) α/2 (JEE Main 2025 Online, 2nd April Morning Shift) —

A circular disk of radius R meter and mass M kg is rotating around the axis perpendicular to the disk. An external torque is applied to the disk such that θ(t) = 5t² − 8t, where θ(t) is the angular position of the rotating disc as a function of time t. How much power is delivered by the applied torque, when t = 2s? (a) 60MR² (b) 72MR² (c) 8MR² (d) 108MR² (JEE Main 2025 Online, 23rd January Evening Shift) —

A solid sphere of mass m and radius r is allowed to roll without slipping from the highest point of an inclined plane of length L and makes an angle 30° with the horizontal. The speed of the particle at the bottom of the plane is v 1 . If the angle of inclination is increased to 45° while keeping L constant. Then the new speed of the sphere at the bottom of the plane is v 2 . The ratio v 1 ² : v 2 ² is (a) 1 : 3 (b) 1 : 2 (c) 1 : √2 (d) 1 : √3 (JEE Main 2025 Online, 23rd January Morning Shift) —

answer: c B, C, D and E only
stem: Which of the following are correct expression for torque acting on a body? (A) τ̄ = r̄ × L̄ (B) τ̄ = (d/dt)(r̄ × p̄) (C) τ̄ = r̄ × dp̄/dt (D) τ̄ = Iᾱ (E) τ̄ = r̄ × F̄. (r̄ = position vector, p̄ = linear momentum, L̄ = angular momentum, ᾱ = angular acceleration, I = moment of inertia, F̄ = force, t = time) Choose the correct answer from the options given below : (a) A, B, C and E only (b) C and D only (c) B, C, D and E only (d) B, D and E only (JEE Main 2025 Online, 4th April Morning Shift) —
book_key: c B, C, D and E only

stem: A square Lamina OABC of length 10 cm is pivoted at O. Forces act at Lamina as shown in figure (10 N up at C, 10 N up at B, 10 N right at B, 10 N right at A, 10 N down at A, and F directed left at C). If Lamina remains stationary, then the magnitude of F is : (a) 10 N (b) 0 (zero) (c) 10√2 N (d) 20 N (JEE Main 2025 Online, 2nd April Morning Shift) —

A cord of negligible mass is wound around the rim of a wheel supported by spokes with negligible mass. The mass of wheel is 10 kg and radius is 10 cm and it can freely rotate without any friction. Initially the wheel is at rest. If a steady pull of 20 N is applied on the cord, the angular velocity of the wheel, after the cord is unwound by 1 m, would be : (a) 20 rad/s (b) 30 rad/s (c) 10 rad/s (d) 0 rad/s (JEE Main 2025 Online, 2nd April Morning Shift) —
